Based on my search, here are the key food temperature standards for accepting, storing, and handling food safely:

## Temperature Danger Zone

The most critical concept in food safety is the **"temperature danger zone"** where bacteria grow rapidly:

- **USDA/ServSafe standard:** 40°F to 140°F (4°C to 60°C)
- **Australian/New Zealand standard:** 5°C to 60°C (41°F to 140°F)

Food should **NOT** be kept in this temperature range for extended periods. Bacteria can double every 20 minutes within this zone.

---

## Accepting and Receiving Food Temperatures

When accepting food deliveries:

| Food Type | Safe Temperature |
|-----------|----------------|
| **Cold/refrigerated foods** | 40°F (4°C) or below |
| **Frozen foods** | 0°F (-18°C) or below |
| **Hot foods** | 135°F (57°C) or above |

---

## Safe Holding Temperatures

| Category | Temperature Requirement |
|----------|------------------------|
| **Cold holding** | 40°F (4°C) or below |
| **Hot holding** | 135°F (57°C) or above |
| **Frozen storage** | 0°F (-18°C) or below |

---

## Safe Cooking/Internal Temperatures

| Food Type | Minimum Internal Temperature |
|-----------|------------------------------|
| Poultry, stuffing, dishes with cooked TCS foods | 165°F (74°C) |
| Ground meat, injected meats, eggs held for service | 155°F (68°C) |
| Seafood, steaks, chops, roasts | 145°F (63°C) |
| Vegetables, fruits, grains, legumes | 135°F (57°C) |
| Reheated food | 165°F (74°C) |

---

## Key Time Limits

- **Cold food without refrigeration:** Maximum 6 hours (starting from 40°F), if it doesn't exceed 70°F
- **Hot food below 135°F:** Discard after 4 hours
- **Perishable food at room temperature:** Maximum 2 hours (1 hour if above 90°F ambient temperature)

---

## International Standards Summary

| Region | Cold Storage | Hot Holding | Danger Zone |
|--------|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| **United States (FDA/USDA)** | ≤40°F (4°C) | ≥135°F (57°C) | 40°F–140°F |
| **Australia/New Zealand** | ≤5°C (41°F) | ≥60°C (140°F) | 5°C–60°C |
| **European Union** | ≤4°C (39°F) | — | Similar range |
| **WHO/HACCP (international)** | ≤10°C (50°F) | ≥65°C (149°F) | 10°C–65°C |

---

## Important Tips

1. **Always use a calibrated food thermometer** — never rely on appearance, color, or touch
2. **Check temperatures every 2 hours** for foods being held
3. **Reject deliveries** that arrive outside safe temperature ranges
4. **Document temperatures** for regulatory compliance and HACCP programs
5. **Never accept food** that has been in the danger zone for unknown periods

Sources:
1. https://www.webstaurantstore.com/article/29/following-food-safety-temperatures.html?srsltid=AfmBOoq2fbzrXzcsShexiv5vVjGqq3ZYhHjZMIjcXI5fohCAZ4JqUr7f
2. https://thermalog.com.au/australian-food-safety-standards-a-guide-to-temperature-compliance/
3. https://www.coohom.com/article/industry-standards-for-room-temperature-in-food-and-laboratory-settings
4. https://spice.alibaba.com/spice-basics/what-temperature-to-cook-sausage
5. https://spice.alibaba.com/spice-basics/temp-to-cook-sausage
6. https://www.rotomouldedproducts.com/news/what-are-the-key-temperature-requirements-for-safe-food-transportation-according-to-international-st-244097.html
7. https://ladle.com/resources/blog/safe-food-temperatures-protect-public-health-and-your-bottom-line/

9. https://www.tempcontrolpack.com/knowledge/temperature-standards-for-coldchain-logistics/
